title: Numbers & Functions
summary: A function assigns exactly one output to each input. Functions are described by tables, formulas, graphs, or words, and live on a domain of allowed inputs. Interval notation names sets of real numbers compactly.

function.plain: A rule giving exactly one output per input.
function.in_class: Passes the vertical line test on a graph.

domain.in_class: Exclude values causing division by zero or even roots of negatives.

independent variable.in_class: You choose it freely within the domain.

interval notation.plain: A compact way to write a set of numbers.

vertical line test.plain: A graph is a function if no vertical line hits it twice.

relation.plain: Any pairing of inputs and outputs.
relation.in_class: A function is a special relation.

concept_sections.heading: What a function is
concept_sections.explanation: A function assigns each input exactly one output. The same input can't produce two different outputs — that's the defining rule.
math_steps: Check each input has one output.
Two outputs for one input ⇒ not a function.
On a graph, use the vertical line test.

concept_sections.heading: Four representations
concept_sections.explanation: Functions appear as tables, formulas, graphs, and verbal descriptions. Being fluent in translating among them is essential.
math_steps: Read the function from any form.
Convert between table, formula, graph, words.

concept_sections.heading: Domain and range
concept_sections.explanation: The domain is the set of valid inputs; the range is the set of resulting outputs. Exclude inputs that break the formula (zero denominators, negative even-roots).
math_steps: Find inputs that break the rule.
Determine the outputs for the range.

concept_sections.heading: Interval notation
concept_sections.explanation: Write sets of numbers as intervals: brackets include an endpoint, parentheses exclude it, and $\infty$ always gets a parenthesis.

concept_sections.heading: The vertical line test
concept_sections.explanation: A graph represents a function exactly when no vertical line crosses it more than once — guaranteeing one output per input.
math_steps: Scan vertical lines across the graph.
More than one hit ⇒ not a function.
